Unit 9 – Grammar

Conditionals · 10 exercises · Click a tab to start

Exercise A – Write Yes or No
Answer the questions about each conditional sentence by writing Yes or No.
1. If Carl doesn't come to the party, I'll be really upset.
Is it possible that Carl won't come to the party?
✓ Yes (first conditional → real/possible future)
2. If my neighbour became prime minister, he'd give everyone a million euros.
Is it likely that the neighbour will become prime minister?
Is it possible that the neighbour will become prime minister?
✓ No (unlikely) / Yes (remotely possible – second conditional)
3. If Helen weren't here, I don't know what we'd do.
Is Helen here now?
✓ No – Helen is NOT here (second conditional = hypothetical, contrary to fact… wait: "weren't here" implies she IS here)
4. If Tarek had had enough money, he'd have bought a car.
Did Tarek have enough money?
Did he buy a car?
✓ No / No (third conditional = past unreal: he didn't have money, didn't buy car)
5. If Debbie hadn't gone to the UK, she wouldn't have met Will.
Did Debbie go to the UK?
Did she meet Will?
✓ Yes / Yes (third conditional: she DID go, she DID meet Will)
6. If the police had investigated the case thoroughly, they wouldn't have arrested Keren.
Did the police investigate the case thoroughly?
Did they arrest Keren?
✓ No / Yes (they didn't investigate properly, so they DID arrest Keren)
7. Had she not gone to university, she might not have started her own business.
Did she go to university?
Did she start her own business?
✓ Yes / Yes (inverted third conditional: she DID go, she DID start a business)

Use the zero conditional to complete each definition. Write your own answer for each gap.
  • 1. If you bully someone,
    Example: you use your power to hurt or frighten them
  • 2. If you accuse someone,
    Example: you say that they have done something wrong
  • 3. If you are a liar,
    Example: you regularly say things that are not true
  • 4. If you are rich,
    Example: you have a lot of money and possessions
  • 5. If you are lucky,
    Example: good things happen to you by chance
  • 6. If you are lazy,

Exercise C – Complete using the correct form of the verbs in the box
Use each verb once in the correct form to complete the first conditional sentences.
be · call · find · forget · get · leave · see · take · want · work
  • 1. If she at five o'clock, she'll be there by half past seven.
    ✓ leaves (first conditional: if + present simple)
  • 2. We you if we have any problems.
    ✓ call (will + bare infinitive in main clause — 'll call)
  • 3. It might not be a good idea to go out tonight if you an important test in the morning.
    ✓ have (if + present simple)
  • 4. If you ill all day, you shouldn't come to the club tonight.
    ✓ are / feel (if + present simple)
  • 5. If you should my wallet, call me on my mobile immediately!
    ✓ find (if + should + bare infinitive = formal first conditional)
  • 6. Let's get a different DVD if you that one already.
    ✓ have seen / 've seen (if + present perfect for completed action)
  • 7. If Sean so hard lately, he'll welcome the chance to have a few days off.
    ✓ has been working / 's been working (if + present perfect continuous)
  • 8. If you're going into town, a video for tonight while you're there!
    ✓ take (imperative in main clause is also possible in first conditional)
  • 9. If you see Carol tonight, to say hello from me!
    ✓ want (remember to / don't forget to say hello)
  • 10. Don't feel you have to come if you don't to.
    ✓ want (if you don't want to = zero/first conditional)
Exercise D – Circle the correct word or phrase
Choose the correct conditional conjunction in bold.
  • 1. This time in six months I'll be at university I decide to take a year off first.
    ✓ unless (= except if I decide to take a year off)
  • 2. We'd better leave early tomorrow there's a lot of traffic when we get to Doncaster.
    ✓ in case (we prepare for the possibility of traffic)
  • 3. You can watch the film you promise to go straight to bed when it finishes.
    ✓ as long as (= on the condition that)
  • 4. Let's go to Mirabella's tonight you haven't been there before.
    ✓ if (= on the condition that you haven't been there)
  • 5. I've still got my health, I don't mind how poor I am!
    ✓ So long as (= provided that I have my health)
  • 6. You'd better take a sweater with you now it gets cold tonight.
    ✓ in case (take a sweater as a precaution)
  • 7. Do what you like you don't make any noise.
    ✓ provided (= on condition that you don't make noise)
  • 8. I'm not going to worry she hasn't called by midnight.
    ✓ unless (= I won't worry except if she hasn't called)
Exercise E – Write sentences using the second conditional
Rewrite each idea as a second conditional sentence. Use the example as a guide.
Example: I don't want to buy that CD so I'm not going to. → If I wanted to buy that CD, I would.
  • 1.
    I don't live alone so I don't get lonely.
    ✓ If I lived alone, I would get lonely.
  • 2.
    Don's got such a lot of homework that he's not going to play football tonight.
    ✓ If Don didn't have so much homework, he'd play football tonight.
  • 3.
    I can't swim so I'm not going scuba diving with Terry.
    ✓ If I could swim, I'd go scuba diving with Terry.
  • 4.
    We're not going to order a pizza because we don't have enough money.
    ✓ If we had enough money, we'd order a pizza.
  • 5.
    We're not staying in the same hotel, so we can't share a room.
    ✓ If we were staying in the same hotel, we could share a room.
  • 6.
    I'm not you, but I think you should call Antony right now!
    ✓ If I were you, I'd call Antony right now!
  • 7.
    I can't come because I have to help my dad with something.
    ✓ If I didn't have to help my dad, I could / would come.
  • 8.
    I don't go to bed as late as you so I'm able to get up early in the morning.
    ✓ If I went to bed as late as you, I wouldn't be able to get up early.

Based on the text about parallel universes, complete each third conditional sentence.
  • 1. If I'd started learning English a year earlier,

  • 2. If a meteor hadn't struck the Earth,
    ✓ the dinosaurs wouldn't have become extinct.
  • 3. If my best friend had won the lottery last summer,
    ✓ he/she would have moved to a bigger house.
  • 4. If my parents
    ✓ If my parents hadn't met, I wouldn't have been born.
  • 5. Everyone on board the Titanic
    ✓ Everyone on board the Titanic would have survived (if there had been enough lifeboats).
  • 6. Van Gogh (if he had been recognised during his lifetime).
    ✓ Van Gogh wouldn't have died in poverty.
  • 7. Madonna (if she hadn't been discovered).
    ✓ Madonna wouldn't have made any records.
  • 8. If George Bush
    ✓ If George Bush hadn't become President, … (open answer based on text)
  • 9. If Greece
    ✓ If Greece hadn't won the European Cup in July 2004, … (open answer)
Exercise G – Choose the correct answer
Choose the best option A, B, C or D for each gap in the passage about parallel universes.

If this theory about parallel universes (1) correct, it (2) that we're living in more than one universe at the same time. But if that (3) true – if I was doing different things in different universes – (4) about it. And if I (5) about it, how could it be me doing these things? If I (6) the lottery last year in a parallel universe, and decided to sail round the world, how is that 'me'? It doesn't make sense!

And another thing. If I do something, it (7) consequences. For example, if I (8) study, I might not pass my exams. I can't start thinking about different universes where the consequences are different. If I just (9) about the universe I actually live in, then I'm sure (10) okay!

Options:
1: A will be  B is  C would have been  D has been
2: A has meant  B meant  C had meant  D means
3: A will be  B was being  C were  D has been
4: A I'd know  B I'll know  C I have known  D I know
5: A wouldn't know  B don't know  C won't know  D didn't know
6: A had won  B was winning  C have won  D win
7: A would have  B would have had  C will have  D had had
8: A won't  B haven't  C don't  D hadn't
9: A think  B to think  C am thinking  D have thought
10: A I'd be  B I've been  C I'd have been  D I'll be
✓ (1) B  (2) D  (3) C  (4) A  (5) A  (6) C  (7) A  (8) C  (9) A  (10) A
Exercise H – Complete using the correct form of the verbs in brackets
Use mixed conditionals (second/third) and complete both gaps where needed.
  • 1. If (you / do) your homework last night, you'd know the answer to this question!
    ✓ you had done (mixed conditional: past condition → present result)
  • 2a. We (not / stand) by the side of the road at the moment trying to get a lift
    ✓ wouldn't be standing
  • 2b. if (we / bring) a spare tyre with us.
    ✓ we had brought / we'd brought
  • 3a. If I (not / stay up) so late last night,
    ✓ hadn't stayed up
  • 3b. I (not / feel) so tired this morning!
    ✓ wouldn't feel (mixed: past condition → present result)
  • 4a. (I / be) in terrible trouble right now
    ✓ I'd be (present result)
  • 4b. if you (not / help) me.
    ✓ hadn't helped (past condition)
  • 5. If I had a video recorder, (I / record) the match last night.
    ✓ I would have recorded (mixed: present condition → past result)
  • 6a. (I / ask) for Andy's phone number when I met him
    ✓ I would have asked
  • 6b. if (not / already / have) a boyfriend!
    ✓ I hadn't already had / I didn't already have
  • 7a. If Cody (not / live) so far away,
    ✓ didn't live
  • 7b. he (not / be) so late to the barbecue yesterday.
    ✓ wouldn't have been (mixed: present condition → past result)
  • 8a. Tracy (not / need) extra lessons last month
    ✓ wouldn't have needed
  • 8b. if she (be) as good at maths as you are.
    ✓ were / was (mixed: present condition → past result)
  • 9a. (you / got) a job when you left school
    ✓ Would you have got
  • 9b. if the university (not / offer) you a place?
    ✓ hadn't offered
  • 10a. If you (have) as much money as she does,
    ✓ had (second conditional condition)
  • 10b. (you / retire) by now?
    ✓ would you retire / would you have retired
Exercise I – Complete the sentences so that the meaning remains the same
Rewrite each sentence using inverted conditional form (Should / Were / Had …).
  • 1.
    If her condition should improve, we'll inform you immediately.
    Should
    ✓ Should her condition improve, we'll inform you immediately.
  • 2.
    Jade will ask lots of difficult questions if she gets to interview a famous politician.
    Should
    ✓ Should Jade get to interview a famous politician, she will ask lots of difficult questions.
  • 3.
    If you were able to go abroad for the summer, where would you go?
    Were
    ✓ Were you able to go abroad for the summer, where would you go?
  • 4.
    If I was to become a vet, I'd find putting animals down very difficult.
    Were
    ✓ Were I to become a vet, I'd find putting animals down very difficult.
  • 5.
    The world would be much better off if all environmental pollution stopped today.
    Were
    ✓ Were all environmental pollution to stop today, the world would be much better off.
  • 6.
    If the hole in the ozone layer had been discovered sooner, fewer people would have got skin cancer.
    Had
    ✓ Had the hole in the ozone layer been discovered sooner, fewer people would have got skin cancer.
  • 7.
    I wouldn't have become a teacher if I hadn't had such a good English teacher at school.
    Had
    ✓ Had I not had such a good English teacher at school, I wouldn't have become a teacher.
